gaps.name: Open a Saved Messages topic as a real chat
gaps.whatItIs: Modern Telegram opens a saved topic in the full chat controller scoped to saved_messages_topic_id (SavedMessagesScreen pushes a ChatController with a saved-messages subject), with bubbles, media, reply, forward, selection and a composer.
gaps.whyItMatters: Our topic screen (TGSavedMessagesViewController.m, the inner topic list controller) is a read-only one-line-per-message text table. Tapping a topic offers only 'open the whole Saved Messages chat' unfiltered, so a user who forwarded a photo album from one person cannot view, forward or delete it inside its topic.
gaps.whereItGoes: TGChatViewController.m needs a topicId-scoped loading path (getSavedMessagesTopicHistory instead of getChatHistory); TGSavedMessagesViewController.m pushes it instead of its private message table.
tdlib: setChatDraftMessage with messageTopicSavedMessages - wrapped as -setSavedMessagesTopic:draftText:completion:, currently unused

gaps.name: Tag filter strip inside the Saved Messages chat
gaps.whatItIs: In the modern client the saved chat itself carries a horizontal chip rail of reaction tags with counts and labels directly under the title; tapping a chip filters the visible message stream to that tag.
gaps.whyItMatters: We only expose tags in two detours: the global search screen (TGSearchViewController.m builds the chip strip and calls searchSavedMessages) and a standalone tags list screen. Inside Saved Messages itself there is no way to say 'show me the ones I tagged Work'; the user has to leave the chat.
gaps.whereItGoes: TGChatViewController.m, reusing the chip-strip code already written in TGSearchViewController.m rebuildTagStrip and the searchSavedMessages request path.
tdlib: getSavedMessagesTags - used raw in TGSearchViewController.m, the declared wrapper -savedMessagesTagsForTopic:completion: does not actually exist in TGClient+SavedMessages
searchSavedMessages - used raw in TGSearchViewController.m, no wrapper despite headers referencing one

gaps.name: Add / rename a tag from the message itself
gaps.whatItIs: Long-pressing a message in Saved Messages offers 'Tag' with an emoji chooser, and a tap on the tag chip under a bubble offers renaming it (SavedTagNameAlertController), so tag labels are created where they are used.
gaps.whyItMatters: Reactions in the self-chat are tags, and our reaction picker does add them, but nothing in the chat tells the user that, the chip renders as a bare reaction with no label, and renaming is only reachable from the separate tags screen. Tags stay invisible unless you already know they exist.
gaps.whereItGoes: TGChatViewController.m message action sheet plus the reaction chip view; rename alert already implemented in TGSavedMessagesTagsViewController.m askRenameForEmoji.

gaps.name: Search scoped to one saved topic
gaps.whatItIs: Modern search inside a saved topic passes the topic id to searchSavedMessages, so query and tag filtering apply within the one author's stream.
gaps.whyItMatters: Our search always passes saved_messages_topic_id 0 (TGSearchViewController.m loadTaggedSavedMessagesPage), so 'that link Anna sent me' has to be found among every saved message ever.
gaps.whereItGoes: TGSearchViewController.m - carry a topicId alongside _scopedChatId; entry point is a search button on the topic screen.
tdlib: searchSavedMessages with saved_messages_topic_id - used raw, no wrapper

gaps.name: Jump to date inside Saved Messages
gaps.whatItIs: A fast-scroll date bubble and date picker backed by sparse message positions, letting you land on a month in a years-deep archive.
gaps.whyItMatters: Saved Messages is the one chat people scroll years back in. We wrapped both calls and never used them: -savedMessagesSparsePositionsForTopic:... and -savedMessagesTopic:messageAtDate: have zero call sites outside TGClient+SavedMessages.m.
gaps.whereItGoes: The topic chat / Saved Messages chat screen; a 'Jump to date' row in the chat action sheet is the cheap version of the scroll bubble.

gaps.name: tg://saved deep link routing
gaps.whatItIs: internalLinkTypeSavedMessages opens the Saved Messages chat when a tg://saved or t.me link is tapped.
gaps.whyItMatters: The predicate -linkOpensSavedMessages:completion: is implemented in TGClient+SavedMessages.m line 512 and called from nowhere, so such a link currently falls through the link dispatcher and does nothing.
gaps.whereItGoes: The link-type dispatch in TGClient+WebLinks.m / the URL open path in AppDelegate.m and TGChatViewController.m link sheet - one extra case that pushes TGSavedMessagesViewController.

gaps.name: Clear a topic's messages by date range
gaps.whatItIs: Modern offers deleting only part of a saved topic between two dates rather than wiping it.
gaps.whyItMatters: Today the only destructive option on a topic row is delete-everything, which is a scary all-or-nothing on an archive people keep for years.
gaps.whereItGoes: TGSavedMessagesViewController.m topic long-press action sheet, next to the existing delete confirmation (kSavedDeleteAlertTag).

gaps.name: Quick reply shortcuts
gaps.whatItIs: Named canned-message shortcuts (Settings > Business > Quick Replies in QuickReplySetupScreen.swift): create, rename, reorder and delete a shortcut, edit the messages it contains in a chat-like editor, and send it into any chat by typing '/name' in the composer.
gaps.whyItMatters: Typing the same reply repeatedly on a 4S keyboard is exactly the case where a shortcut pays off, and shortcuts created on a desktop client are invisible and unsendable here today.
gaps.whereItGoes: New shortcut list screen reachable from TGSettingsViewController.m, plus a '/' suggestion row in the existing mention/hashtag suggestion strip in TGChatViewController.m.
tdlib: deleteQuickReplyShortcut, setQuickReplyShortcutName, reorderQuickReplyShortcuts, checkQuickReplyShortcutName - not wrapped

gaps.name: Custom emoji tags
gaps.whatItIs: Premium users tag saved messages with animated custom emoji, rendered as animated chips on bubbles and in the tag rail.
gaps.whyItMatters: Tags set from a desktop premium account would show as blanks here, but plain-emoji tags cover the feature for practical use.
gaps.whereItGoes: Would be the reaction chip renderer in TGChatViewController.m; recommend a static fallback glyph rather than support.
